HOME HEALTH SKILLED NURSING / SPEECH THERAPY VISIT NOTE

Patient: 78-year-old female with history of ischemic stroke (right MCA, 4 months ago) complicated by moderate oropharyngeal dysphagia, on thickened liquids and mechanical soft diet. Referred for home health services including skilled speech-language pathology for dysphagia management with surface electrical stimulation as an adjunct to swallowing exercises.

Physician of record: Dr. R. Alvarez, Internal Medicine, is following patient closely and directing the plan of care. Face-to-face encounter was completed by Dr. Alvarez 12 days prior to start of home health care, documenting continued dysphagia, aspiration risk, and need for skilled therapy in the home setting.

Homebound status: Patient requires assistance of two persons and a rolling walker to ambulate short distances within the home; leaving the home requires considerable and taxing effort and is limited to medical appointments accompanied by family. Confinement to home is clearly documented in the intake assessment and nursing notes.

Plan of care: Established plan of care was signed and dated by Dr. Alvarez at start of care, outlining frequency and duration of SLP visits (3x/week for 4 weeks), goals for improved swallow safety, and inclusion of neuromuscular electrical stimulation to the anterior neck musculature as an adjunct to traditional dysphagia exercises.

Today's visit: SLP performed skilled swallow evaluation and applied surface electrical stimulation electrodes to the submental and infrahyoid region per plan of care, in conjunction with effortful swallow exercises and Mendelsohn maneuver training. Patient tolerated treatment well, mild improvement noted in hyolaryngeal excursion on palpation. Skilled intervention is necessary given complexity of dysphagia management, risk of aspiration pneumonia, and need for professional judgment in electrode placement and stimulation parameters, all clearly documented in the chart.

The initial certification period began 8 weeks ago. Chart review today shows the physician's recertification of the home health plan of care was completed and signed on day 75 of the certification period, beyond the 60-day interval required for continuing home care. No recertification documentation exists for days 61-74; the agency continued to provide skilled visits during this gap based on the original plan alone. This delay was noted during today's chart audit and flagged for follow-up with the physician's office; however, as of today's visit no recertification had yet been signed within the required 60-day window.

All documentation, including evaluation notes, treatment logs, and physician communications, remains legible and stored in the patient's electronic medical record, available for MAC review upon request.

Plan: Continue skilled SLP visits, obtain corrected recertification from physician's office, reassess swallow function next visit.
